comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find the transcriptomic and proteomic analyses (C1-C6, C9-C10) convincing and well-supported. OpenEval notes 'converging multi-omics evidence' while peer reviewers explicitly praised these as 'invaluable information to the field.' Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Significant disagreement. OpenEval rates C32-C34 (TAB2 recruitment persisting despite E1 inhibitor) as SUPPORTED, calling it 'appropriately characterized' mechanistic insight. Peer Reviewer 4 rates as UNCERTAIN, stating 'authors need to clarify whether TAB2 is or is not recruited in the GPN/DC661 conditions' and noting the mechanism remains incompletely understood.

Disagreement on certainty level. OpenEval rates C35-C40 (differential responses to damage inducers) as SUPPORTED with 'appropriately inferred' mechanistic interpretation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 4 requesting clarification on TAB2 recruitment and noting 'unresolved questions about damage type specificity.'

Complete agreement. Both evaluations find C41-C53 (transcriptome analysis with genetic perturbations, TFEB independence) convincing and well-supported. OpenEval notes 'converging evidence' while peer reviewers stated findings were 'convincingly demonstrated' with 'compelling experiments.' Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Complete agreement. Both evaluations find C80-C83 (pathway-dependent gene expression via RT-qPCR) well-supported. OpenEval notes 'convergence of pharmacological and genetic approaches' while peer reviewers accepted the demonstration of 'transcriptional upregulation of pro-inflammatory genes.' Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Complete agreement. Both evaluations find C84-C90 (anti-apoptotic function via multiple approaches) convincingly demonstrated. OpenEval notes 'critical anti-apoptotic function' while peer reviewers stated this was 'successfully achieved' and 'convincingly demonstrated.' Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Complete agreement. Both evaluations find C91-C95 (paracrine signaling via conditioned media) supported. OpenEval notes 'appropriate experimental design' while peer reviewers accepted the demonstration of 'intercellular signal transduction' and 'cell-cell communication.' Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Complete agreement. Both evaluations find C59-C70 (IKK-IκBα pathway activation) well-supported. OpenEval notes 'canonical pathway activation downstream of TAK1' while peer reviewers stated the 'TAB, TAK1, and IKK axis culminating in NF-κB activation' was 'convincingly shown.' Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Complete agreement. Both evaluations find C54-C58 (MAPK phosphorylation via phosphoproteome analysis) supported. OpenEval notes 'TAK1-dependent increases' with appropriate citations, while peer reviewers accepted TAK1 as 'essential for MAP kinase signaling.' Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Complete agreement. Both evaluations endorse C96-C98, C154-C155 (major findings summary) as well-supported. OpenEval notes 'comprehensive multi-omics, biochemical, and functional data' while editor and reviewers stated 'major aims successfully achieved' and findings are 'important.' Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Complete agreement. Both evaluations find C71-C79 (TBK1/LUBAC positioning downstream of TAK1) supported. Complete agreement. Both evaluations find C27-C31 (TAB2/TAK1 activation mechanism via K63 ubiquitin) well-supported. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Peer reviewers rate overlapping claims (C125-C126, C156) as UNCERTAIN, stating these are 'speculative proposals requiring further validation.' Both recognize these as hypotheses.

Peer reviewers rate overlapping claims (C118-C120, C123) as UNCERTAIN, stating these are 'speculative interpretations' with gaps indicated by Reviewer 4's concerns.
